description: Neutral keyboard-slot grammar of the one-shortcut model (docs/design/one-shortcut-model.md, PAR-41 step 2). A slot id is zero or more modifier ROLES in the fixed order of "modifier_order", then one key id of modifier_chords.json, joined by underscores (primary_g, primary_shift_v, meta_space). A role names what the modifier does, not what it is called: "primary" is the main command modifier. Each role lists the modifier id every driver calls it (the ids of modifier_chords.json platforms), or null with the reason when the driver's keyboard has no such key. tools/test/test-slot-roles-single-source.cjs holds the table to modifier_chords.json and to the drivers' slot prefix families; tools/codegen/codegen-slot-roles.cjs projects it to _shared/lua/shortcuts/slot_roles_data.lua. "families" lists, per driver and in menu order, the role combinations under which that driver accepts any key; "extra_keys" are keys a driver accepts in slots that modifier_chords.json (which also feeds the chord actions of every driver) does not carry.

secondary.meaning: The control modifier a Mac keyboard keeps besides Cmd.
secondary.absent_reason: Windows and Linux already use Ctrl as the primary modifier; they have no second control key.

meta.meaning: The operating-system key (Windows key, Super key).
meta.absent_reason: A Mac keyboard has no operating-system key besides Cmd, which is the primary modifier.
